title: Finite length from finite maximal support
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and Q an R-module. For a maximal ideal m let Q_m be its localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], regarded as an R_m-module. Suppose S is a finite set of maximal ideals, Q_m is zero for every maximal ideal outside S, and Q_m has finite length over R_m [def-weil-pbc-module-length] for every m in S. Then Q has finite length over R.

source.place: Tag 00PF, final local-to-global implication; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00PF. The lattice proof of the finite-support generalization is written by K4.

proof.text: For every submodule N of Q take its localizations at the maximal ideals in S, defined by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. This defines a monotone map from Submodule R Q to the finite product of the local submodule lattices.

This map reflects inclusion. If localized N is contained in localized P at every ideal in S, it is also contained at ideals outside S since those local modules are zero. Localization at all maximal ideals detects membership: for q not in P, the proper ideal {a : a q lies in P} is contained in a maximal ideal m, and q/1 cannot lie in P_m since clearing denominators would give an element outside m in that ideal. Apply this to every element of N. Mathlib Submodule.le_of_localization_maximal implements this test. Thus the map is an order embedding.

Each local submodule lattice has ascending and descending chain conditions because its module has finite length [def-weil-pbc-module-length], by Module.length_ne_top_iff and isFiniteLength_iff_isNoetherian_isArtinian. A finite pointwise product of such lattices has both chain conditions (Pi.wellFoundedLT, also applied to the dual lattices). Order embeddings inherit both chain conditions. Thus Q is Noetherian and Artinian, and Module.length_ne_top gives finite length. The empty product case is included.
